title: Bug: HTTP methods in CORS preflight response are lowercase, causing browser rejection
description:
The `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` header returned in OPTIONS preflight requests contains HTTP methods in lower case (for instance `delete`), which causes browsers to reject requests for the methods, even when they are properly configured.

## Current behavior

I built a reproducible example here: https://github.com/CharlesBordet/firesafety-issue-8

When you click on the [Call API] button, the browser runs an OPTIONS Preflight request, which runs successfully (status 204) and returns this response header:

```
access-control-allow-methods: get,head,put,patch,post,delete
```

The browser then doesn't run the DELETE request because it considers that it doesn't belong to the allowed methods.

On Firefox:

```
Cross-Origin Request Blocked: The Same Origin Policy disallows reading the remote resource at http://127.0.0.1:14361/echo. (Reason: Did not find method in CORS header ‘Access-Control-Allow-Methods’)
Cross-Origin Request Blocked: The Same Origin Policy disallows reading the remote resource at http://127.0.0.1:14361/echo. (Reason: CORS request did not succeed). Status code: (null).
```

On Chromium:

```
Access to fetch at 'http://127.0.0.1:14361/echo' from origin 'http://127.0.0.1:5092' has been blocked by CORS policy: Method DELETE is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Methods in preflight response.
```

I observed the same issue with DELETE and PATCH methods. There is no issue for GET and POST methods (browsers might be more flexible with these methods).

## Expected behavior

The `self$add_path()` method shouldn't change the case of the `methods` argument. Or even force them to be uppercase rather than lowercase.

## Proposed fix

I tried changing the methods to uppercase in the case (in `R/CORS.R` and in `R/aaa.R` but the API was not working at all after that).

Adding a `toupper` in `R/CORS.R#213` also seems to do the trick.

title: Consider adding permission policy to security headers
Consider rate limiter plugin
description:
- Implement request rate limiting to protect against brute force attacks and DoS attempts
- Allow configuration of limits per IP, path, or user
- Include options for different response behaviors when limits are exceeded (block, delay, challenge)

title: Easy-to-use protection from cross-site request forgery (CSRF)
